message:
Francois, I'm thinking more of the Turkle who in *Life on the Screen* constructs lived experience as a direct analogue of her title: AIM messaging and F2F are one and the same, and "RL is just another window on my screen". Pathetically Cartesian and middle class in its avoidance of material conditions and proposing that cyberspace is just like real life.

Yeah. On an MIT salary, maybe, especially if you live in Somerville or somewhere nicer and don't worry about rent or month-to-month expenses. I'd suggest folks who don't own computers know all too well the definition of "class", because so-called middle class values *avoid any discussion of materiality*, which is precisely what Turkle does. Those who are sufficiently well-off not to have to worry about the material aspects of their existence, *don't*, and choose to shape their discussions around the life of the mind, around cyberspace, around the immaterial. You talk rent or salary or grocery bills to them, you might as well have farted in church.
